header.text: Subject: [PATCH] Fix: Globally suppress GCC 16+ -Warray-bounds false positives
Switching from local pragma fixes to global suppression for the
The following diagram illustrates why the compiler's static analysis
fails to correctly map the object boundaries in 7-Zip's architecture:
An object (e.g., CHandler) is allocated with a fixed size (N bytes).
The object inherits from multiple interfaces. When accessed via a
specific interface pointer, the "vtable" and "member offsets"
shift relative to the base pointer.
|            |            +-- GCC Flags: "Access here is out of bounds!"
While local pragmas (push/pop) are generally preferred, the recurring
nature of this error across various modules (HandlerCont.cpp,
RarHandler.cpp, FilterCoder.h, etc.) indicates a systemic conflict
between 7-Zip's COM-like architecture and modern GCC's devirtualization
Globally ignoring this specific warning for GCC 16+ is the most
maintainable solution to ensure build stability without refactoring
Ref: GCC Bugzilla #101476 (False positive bounds check in devirt)

Subject: [PATCH 5/5] fix: let a Steam window take global focus under SteamControlled
A Steam client update paints nothing. The panel goes black the moment the
bootstrapper decides an update is due and stays black until the install
finishes — measured 13.5 minutes on HW, with zero atomic flips committed for the
entire window. There is no progress bar, no logo, no backlight change; the
device is indistinguishable from hung, and the natural user response is to hold
The dialog is drawn. `xwininfo` shows it mapped, IsViewable, InputOutput,
opaque, fullscreen, with a live commit queue. It is nonetheless never presented,
because it never becomes the global focus window.
`SteamControlled` (`main.cpp`). That makes `controlledFocus` true for the whole
then withholds the generic `vecPossibleFocusWindows[ 0 ]` fallback from the
global pass. That is intentional and worth keeping: it stops a game window from
taking the screen away from whatever Steam has asked to be frontmost. But it
leaves `focusControlWindow` and `ctxFocusControlAppIDs` as the only two routes
to global focus, and Steam publishes both — so during a client update neither
exists yet. Instrumented on the device, `focusControlWindow` measured `0x0` for
the entire update and `ctxFocusControlAppIDs` measured empty (it only fills in
with `[413091, 769]` once the client proper is up).
The bootstrapper's dialog cannot match either. It carries `STEAM_BIGPICTURE=1`,
so `isSteamLegacyBigPicture` and therefore `window_is_steam()` are true, but it
has no `STEAM_GAME`, so its `appID` is 0 and no control appID can name it — the
same override-redirect window upstream already special-cases elsewhere in
steamcompmgr ("bootstrapper is override redirect :("). It passes every candidate
filter, sorts into `vecPossibleFocusWindows`, and is then dropped for want of a
route. `focus` stays NULL, so `out->focusWindow` is never assigned and nothing is
So add the missing route: when the global pass under `SteamControlled` would
otherwise end with no focus, take the highest-priority candidate for which
The guard is deliberately narrow. It runs only when `focus` is already NULL, so
anything Steam actively asked for has matched first and a live client's choice
can never be overridden. It is restricted to the global pass, so the local pass
keeps reaching the generic fallback exactly as before. It is restricted to
untouched. And it will only ever select a Steam window — never a game — which
preserves precisely the behaviour the withheld fallback exists to protect.
`localGameFocused` is computed the same way the generic fallback computes it
(`focus->appID != 0`), so the bootstrapper correctly does not register as a game
Not sent upstream: on Valve's own hardware the bootstrapper reaches the panel
because its update UI is presented before `--steam` is in play. This is worth
carrying regardless of that, since the failure mode it removes is a device that
looks bricked during a routine update.

Subject: [PATCH] DRMBackend: add --rotated-output-max-height and let the plane
Some display controllers rotate a plane at scanout but only up to a maximum
PRE-ROTATION source height -- 1088 lines on Qualcomm's DPU inline rotator. The
plane advertises ROTATE_90 as a static capability and cannot qualify it per-mode,
so on a portrait panel wider than that limit gamescope takes the capability at
face value, stops rotating in the compositor, and then every atomic commit is
rejected and nothing is ever scanned out. The panel is simply black.
--rotated-output-max-height clamps the LOGICAL output height (aspect preserving,
both axes even) when the panel is scanned out rotated, and scales the resulting
CRTC rects back up to the real mode so the same plane upscales for free. SRC_W/H
stay at the texture size -- the scale is src -> crtc.
Without the flag nothing changes. It applies to 90/270 only: 0/180 do not
transpose, so the source height is the mode's own height and the rotator limit
drm_set_refresh() looks its mode up by the panel's real size when the clamp is
active, since the clamped size matches no mode on the connector and would
otherwise fall through to generating a timing the panel cannot display.

Subject: [PATCH] rtasm: release the executable heap when the driver unloads
The POSIX executable allocator retains a 10 MiB mmap after its suballocations
are freed. When an application closes and reloads the DRI driver (for example,
EmulationStation around each game), the static pointers are lost and a new
heap is mapped each time. Register cleanup with atexit, as other Mesa global
resources do; on our glibc target it also runs when the owning DSO unloads.
Publish the heap only after both allocations succeed, and unwind allocation
or callback-registration failure so a later call can retry. The arena stays
shared and locked during normal operation; no per-shader mmap is introduced.
Downstream: rasteratops/distribution#310. Mesa 26.2.2; current upstream still
has the same unpaired mmap. See docs/qa-logs/2026-10-03-launch-memory/.
Subject: [PATCH] virgl: release an empty screen cache after probe or teardown
The process-global fd table survives a failed virgl probe and the last screen
release. If the driver is unloaded, its pointer is lost. A software-rendered
application that repeatedly reloads Mesa then leaks the empty table each time.
Destroy an empty table under the existing screen mutex, on both paths. Live
screen entries and their sharing/refcounts are unchanged.
Downstream: rasteratops/distribution#310. LeakSanitizer names 592 bytes per
failed software-profile probe at virgl_drm_screen_create in Mesa 26.2.2.

Subject: [PATCH] build: find pre-built heimdal build tools in case of embedded
This patch fixes the case of finding asn1_compile and compile_et for
The Heimdal build tools compile_et and asn1_compile are needed *only*
if we use the embedded heimdal (otherwise we don't build heimdal and
use headers that have been generated by those tools elsewhere).
For cross-compilation with embedded heimdal, it is vital to use host build
tools, and so asn1_compile and compile_et must be supplied and not
built. One way of doing this would be to set the COMPILE_ET and
ASN1_COMPILE env vars to the location of supplied binaries. Another way,
which is more commonly used, is to exclude asn1_compile and compile_et
from bundled packages via the switch
the build script searches the path for those tools and sets the
ASN1_COMPILE and COMPILE_ET vars accordingly. (this is admittedly
kind of a round-about way of doing things but this has become the
de-facto standard amongst embedded distro builders).
finding the binaris has been moved to be carried out only in the

Subject: [PATCH] allwinner: h616: PSCI SYSTEM_SUSPEND via an SRAM stub
From kailashrs' H700_rocknix_enhancement. BL31 copies a stub into SRAM A1
and jumps to it with the MMU off; it puts DRAM into self-refresh, waits
in WFI and re-initialises DRAM on wake without touching its contents.
SUNXI_SUSPEND_STUB2 for a second memory type: one BL31 serves every
bootloader build, so TF-A picks the stub whose DRAM type and clock match
at boot and leaves system suspend unavailable when none does. Unset, the
batteryplus: fall back to voltage_avg when voltage_now is absent
Battery discovery only accepts a supply exposing voltage_now, so in
voltage mode the daemon exits with "No battery voltage path detected"
on PMICs whose driver reports the averaged reading instead. The
handhelds) exposes voltage_avg only. Use voltage_avg when voltage_now
is missing; the averaged value is, if anything, a better input for the
daemon's own smoothing, and unit autodetection is unchanged.
batteryplus: snap the visible percent on resume in PMIC mode
The long-gap snap only exists in voltage mode. In PMIC mode a resume
goes through the ordinary step limiter, which moves one point at a time
and never counts down while charging, so a kernel gauge that corrected
itself across a sleep is hidden from the UI: after a 10 h suspend on an
RG353M the kernel read 63 % while /tmp/battery.percent, and with it ES,
stayed at 87 % because the device woke on the charger.
In PMIC mode the kernel value is the authority and has already done its
own reconciliation; smoothing is there for jitter, not for corrections.
Snap to it whenever a resume is detected.
batteryplus: seed the voltage anchors from the battery driver
The defaults describe a 4.2 V cell (3250/3400 mV empty, 4000/4050 mV
full), so a 4.35 V pack such as the GKD Pixel2's reads 100% from 4.33 V
down to 3.98 V until the first full charge teaches the map otherwise,
and the empty anchors are off for most RK817 packs. The driver already
reports the pack's limits: take voltage_min_design for the empty
anchors, voltage_max_design and constant_charge_voltage_max for the
full ones (voltage_min and voltage_max on axp20x). Empties apply unless
the configuration sets them; full anchors are seeded only while the map
still holds the defaults, so a learned map is never touched.
A charge ceiling learned below the seeded discharge anchor now pulls
that anchor down with it, as the discharge learner already keeps itself
below the ceiling; load_map would otherwise reject the pair.
